extracted.intended_audience: corporate investor-relations/financial PR professionals, regulators, financial journalists, and accounting researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Practical evaluative criteria for drafting and assessing quarterly earnings press releases—especially the use and presentation of non‑GAAP (pro‑forma/adjusted) metrics versus GAAP—based on Bowen, Davis & Matsumoto (2005). Useful for firms, analysts, and journalists judging defensibility and pickup-worthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: GAAP-first ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-Reg‑G, releases must reconcile any non‑GAAP metric with the GAAP equivalent and place the GAAP figure in equal or greater prominence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: "Post‑Reg‑G, releases must reconcile any non‑GAAP metric with the GAAP equivalent and place the GAAP figure in equal or greater prominence. Releases violating this draw SEC comment letters." Practical implication: put GAAP numbers at least as prominently as pro‑forma adjusted numbers and make the reconciliation highly visible to avoid SEC scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline-metric defensibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever earnings metric is in the headline, the release must defend its use over GAAP in the explanatory paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the headline choice is accompanied by a clear, explicit rationale in the body explaining why that metric is informative or preferable for this reporting period (e.g., why certain items were excluded). Avoid leaving the headline metric unsupported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciliation table inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: A clearly labeled reconciliation between any non‑GAAP metric and the closest GAAP equivalent should appear in the release body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a labeled reconciliation table showing how adjusted/pro‑forma figures are derived from GAAP results; make it unambiguous and easy for analysts/journalists to verify adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparable-period basis
rubrics_metrics.description: When emphasizing a metric, use the same metric in prior‑period comparisons; switching basis between periods is flagged by analysts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not change the basis or definition of the comparative metric between quarters when making period‑over‑period statements. If a change is necessary, clearly explain and justify it; otherwise maintain consistent comparators to avoid analyst suspicion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment definition consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Any 'adjusted' metric should use the same definition every quarter; redefining mid‑year is flagged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep adjustment definitions stable across reporting periods. If the definition is altered, disclose the change and its effect on comparatives; arbitrary or mid‑year redefinitions will attract scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis‑vs‑substance audit
rubrics_metrics.description: If the release emphasizes a metric that diverges sharply from GAAP (large one‑time‑charge add‑backs), the release should explain why the adjustment is conceptually appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adjusted figures materially differ from GAAP (e.g., large add‑backs for 'one‑time' charges), provide conceptual justification for treating those items as non‑recurring and for excluding them from performance metrics. Transparency about the nature and rationale for adjustments reduces accusations of misleading emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order‑of‑information consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: The order in which results appear (revenue → operating income → net income → EPS → adjusted EPS) should follow industry convention; reordering to lead with the most flattering line is detectable and gets flagged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow conventional sequencing of financial results. Deliberate reordering to foreground favorable metrics is noticeable to analysts and journalists; adhere to norms unless a clear reason for reordering is disclosed and justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media‑exposure‑bias check
rubrics_metrics.description: High‑media‑exposure firms face greater scrutiny; releases should be drafted assuming sophisticated reading rather than only retail‑investor reception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original observation: "Firms with more media exposure place greater emphasis on pro‑forma earnings than on GAAP — sophisticated PR offices game the press release for media‑friendly framing." Draft releases for analysts and major media (FT, WSJ, Bloomberg, Reuters) who will critically evaluate framing; avoid tactics that rely on uncritical reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pickup‑worthiness: transparency and defensibility
rubrics_metrics.description: At sophisticated outlets, emphasis on a flattering non‑GAAP metric over GAAP triggers analytical scrutiny rather than uncritical reproduction. A pickup‑worthy and defensible earnings release uses non‑GAAP metrics only where they have clear analytical justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical checklist from the paper's implication: (a) use non‑GAAP metrics only with clear analytical justification; (b) reconcile non‑GAAP to GAAP visibly; (c) maintain period‑over‑period definition consistency; (d) favor transparency over flattering framing because major outlets and analysts reward defensibility. Named outlets: FT, WSJ, Bloomberg, Reuters.
